summary:
When the nearest crewmate is 36 million kilometers away, so is the nearest doctor. B.I.P is the full health cabin for long-duration missions: it monitors continuous biosignals (HR, SpO₂, NASA TEPC/CAD-protocol radiation dosimetry, BP and temperature), organizes gamified routines by period with streaks and achievements, and enforces the triage a doctor-less ship demands — onboard kit first, MCC telemedicine second, mission abort last.

At its core is B.I.P, a robot mascot living in the corner of the screen: real conversation (Google Gemini, with a curated offline fallback), reacting to the emotion of your messages — eyes, mouth and antenna shift with sadness, joy, seriousness or danger — and cross-referencing vitals, exams, routine, sleep and chat history when diagnosing symptoms from text or image. It returns probability-ranked hypotheses, an on-board prescription (dose, frequency, duration), red flags and step-by-step conduct.

Also inside: a fully customizable human avatar with reactive emotions, a Mars clock with a real sky and computed Moon phase, a sleep-debt and cognitive-readiness card, and NASA DONKI integration (CMEs and SEP events affecting Mars). Stack: FastAPI + SQLAlchemy, vanilla front-end with inline SVG, Y2K/Frutiger Aero styling in white, petrol teal and terracotta, 38 pytest tests, deployed on Vercel.
details:
In one sentence:
A complete health cabin for astronauts on long-duration missions — an AI companion that monitors vitals, manages routines, diagnoses symptoms, and talks like a friend, tens of millions of kilometers from the nearest doctor.

The problem: When an astronaut is 20 light-minutes away from Earth, the closest physician is 36 million kilometers away. Malaise, insomnia, a headache — today, resolving this relies on high-latency telemedicine, paper manuals, and self-diagnosis. NASA calls human health a pillar of space exploration, but no one had built the interface that a crew member would actually turn to when waking up feeling awful in the dark of the cabin.

The inspiration: The actual routine of ISS crews — daily ARED exercise, TEPC/CAD radiation dosimeters, sleep protocols aligned with cabin lighting, the use of Smart-Tex for continuous monitoring — and one simple question: what if the spacecraft had a copilot dedicated to taking care of you?

What it does:
- Home: Mission dashboard with continuous telemetry (HR, SpO₂, NASA-protocol TEPC/CAD dosimetry, BP, temperature), a sleep card calculating "sleep debt", cognitive readiness, and circadian light synchronization. It includes a Martian clock with a real-time sky and Elena Ricci: a 100% customizable human avatar that reacts to your metrics.

- B.I.P (The Mascot): A robot in the corner of the screen with natural conversation powered by Google Gemini, and a curated offline fallback. It emotionally reacts to your messages — eyes, mouth, and antennas change according to the tone of the conversation. You can talk about anything; if the topic is health, it automatically triggers the medical protocol.

- Routines: A gamified checklist by periods with streaks and achievements. The avatar reacts to your discipline: celebrating when you hit your goals and showing concern when you skip a workout.



- Diagnosis: Accepts text and images. The AI crosses vitals + exams + routine + sleep and returns: probability-based hypotheses, a detailed onboard prescription, and mission triage (Treat onboard → Contact MCC → Abortmission). It only prescribes what actually exists in the spacecraft's medical inventory.




- Exams : A dossier of integrated exams with anomaly alerts.



How we built it: Backend in FastAPI (Python) + SQLAlchemy, with persisted history and anomaly detection via z-score and Mahalanobis distance for circadian baselines. Vanilla frontend without external frameworks, using inline vector SVG for the avatar and mascot, embracing a Y2K / Frutiger Aero aesthetic. AI powered by Gemini with strict JSON schemas. Serverless deployment on Vercel with pytest for testing.

Challenges we overcame: Simulating believable human physiology; ensuring the diagnosis was consistent between the live LLM and the offline engine; designing expressive emotions using pure SVG; and bypassing serverless timeout limits when querying external APIs. Also build an surch responsable system that will help people (probably the only source of information) about your helth.
